rationale: The evidence pack does not document running several attempts of the same task in parallel or comparing their results before choosing one. The multi-agent collaboration and Goal features describe agents working together toward one goal, not parallel competing attempts. Community comparisons to Codex or Conductor describe the UI, not this capability.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run several task attempts in parallel and compare results before choosing one

rationale: ZCode documents its own plugin mechanism: an Excalidraw canvas-collaboration example that covers plugin installation and updates, a page API, and a host integration entry point. That suggests third-party apps can be integrated, but nothing shows partner-built agent apps specifically or how they fit into workflows. missing for 10: evidence of third-party or partner agent apps (not just canvas plugins), a partner ecosystem or marketplace, documentation on wiring plugins into agent workflows, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can integrate third-party partner-built agent apps into my workflows

rationale: ZCode is an AI coding workbench, so a project instructions file for coding standards is a fair question to ask of it. Nothing in the evidence pack documents an AGENTS.md-style rules file, project instructions file, or convention configuration that the agent follows. The only config file mentioned is a local Provider config path (ZCODE_BUILTIN_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE), which is an unrelated setting and earns no credit.

support.subject: As a developer, I can add a project instructions file to set coding standards and conventions the agent follows

rationale: The evidence pack never documents a diff viewer, change review, or running checks or tests before merging in ZCode. The closest item is a claim that Goals plan, execute and verify multi-step work, which is a general agent-workflow claim and not diff inspection or pre-merge checks. A community comment about monitoring file edits in OpenCode is about another product and earns no credit here.

support.subject: As a developer, I can inspect diffs and run checks to catch problems before merging

rationale: Data residency is a fair question for a cloud-backed AI coding workbench, but the evidence shows no option to choose a storage region or jurisdiction. The `ZCODE_DATA_BASE_DIR` variable only sets the local directory for app data. That is an adjacent local-path control, not region or residency selection, so it earns no credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

rationale: The evidence pack has no first-party documentation of a training opt-out, data-usage policy, or privacy control that stops user data from being used to train AI models. Community reports about workspace or git uploads concern data collection, not a training-exclusion control. User-side sandboxing suggestions are workarounds and earn no credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models

rationale: The pack documents no ZCode feature for setting retention periods or deleting stored or uploaded data. `ZCODE_DATA_BASE_DIR` only chooses where local data is written, which is an adjacent control and earns no credit. The note that a new install won't delete existing session data is not a user-facing deletion capability, and the community reports about cloud uploads describe data collection rather than any retention or deletion control.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

rationale: Telemetry opt-out is a fair question for a desktop/terminal AI coding workbench, but nothing in the evidence documents a telemetry or usage-tracking setting, flag, or environment variable. The listed env vars cover provider config and the data directory only. Community reports of silent workspace uploads, and suggestions to sandbox the app or run it under a separate user account, are user-side workarounds and are not a product opt-out.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can opt out of telemetry and usage tracking

rationale: ZCode is an AI coding workbench, so configuring cloud execution environments is a fair question for this kind of product. The evidence pack does not document any cloud environment or way to declare repository dependencies and setup steps. The evidence covers local install, a web UI on a local workspace, SSH/WSL remote projects, and env vars for provider config and data directories; none of these is a reproducible cloud environment, and the community reports about workspace uploads are off-topic.

support.subject: As a developer, I can configure a reproducible cloud environment with the dependencies and setup steps my repository needs

rationale: The pack has no documented debugging capability: nothing on reproducing issues, running or inspecting failing code, or isolating root causes. The closest item is the Goal feature's generic 'planning, execution and verification' of multi-step work (zcode-docs-2). That is an adjacent task-management feature rather than a debugging or fix-verification workflow, so it earns no credit.

support.subject: As a developer, I can reproduce issues, narrow down root causes, and verify fixes

rationale: Sandboxed execution is a fair question for a coding agent, but nothing in the evidence documents a ZCode sandbox for code, tool, or network access. Community reports instead describe it running with full user permissions, and users suggest wrapping it in sandbox-exec or a separate user account. That is a user-side workaround and earns no credit.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can have the agent operate inside a sandbox when interacting with code, tools, and network resources

rationale: ZCode is an AI coding workbench, so a team-shared workspace built from docs and repos is a fair question to ask of it. The evidence only shows `--workspace` pointing the web UI at a single local project directory, plus token-protected LAN access to that UI. That is an adjacent access control, not a documented shared team workspace that combines docs and repos as a common source of truth, so it earns no credit.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can create a shared workspace from my docs and repos as a common source of truth for the team

rationale: The GitHub README documents a terminal Agent and a `zcode` launcher: with no arguments it opens the TUI, `--web` starts a web server, and other arguments are forwarded to the Agent CLI. It does not document a headless, prompt-and-exit, or batch mode for running agent tasks from scripts. The `--web --no-open` flags only launch the web UI server, and chat-app remote triggering is a different feature. Neither counts as non-interactive agent execution for workflow automation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the agent non-interactively in scripts for workflow automation

rationale: A training-data opt-out is a fair axis for an AI coding workbench, but the evidence pack never mentions a model-training policy, privacy setting, or opt-out control for code and prompts. Community reports about workspace uploads describe data transfer, not a training opt-out, and there is no vendor claim for them to contradict. Absence of evidence for an applicable capability yields none.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can opt out of having my code and prompts used for AI model training

rationale: ZCode is documented as an AI coding workbench that spans desktop, browser and terminal-agent interfaces and claims multi-agent collaboration, which glancingly supports a unified place for agent-driven work. Nothing shows a single workspace for viewing, switching between or supervising multiple concurrent coding sessions. Missing for 10: documented multi-session management UI (listing, switching, monitoring parallel sessions), an engineering-lead oversight view, and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can manage multiple agent-driven coding sessions from one unified workspace
